clue.text: Prig on the camera possibly making for film technician

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A priggish crew member fusses over the camera on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of filming and lighting on a movie is a key technician of the craft.

clue.text: Opponent of institution left company after upset, amongst various actions

indicators.note: amongst places the short reversed piece among the rearranged letters
various suggests the letters of actions in a different order
upset, in a down clue, turns the short piece upside down so it reads backwards
after puts company following left

explanation.surface: A rebel against the establishment leaves a firm after a row, among various protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the left-plus-company pair to OCL, which sits 'amongst' the scrambled letters ICONAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast attacks cherished beliefs and established institutions.

clue.text: Understanding regular payment record's not right at either end

indicators.note: an R for right goes from the front of the first piece and the back of the second

parts.note: rent is paid regularly to a landlord
to enter is to record, as in a ledger

explanation.surface: A tenancy deal and its paperwork must be squared away at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: RENT loses its leading R and ENTER its final R, giving ENT + ENTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, an understanding.

clue.text: Father turned up in time, with surprised expression

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, reads the word for father from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad shows up on time, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape describes a mouth hanging open in wonder or shock.

clue.text: Confess immediately, though keeping name till later

indicators.note: keeping, with till later, means holding a letter back to the end of the word
till later says the held letter turns up afterwards, at the end

parts.note: now means immediately

explanation.surface: Someone owns up straight away, though holds back naming names.
explanation.walkthrough: The N of NOW is held back to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up, or own, is to admit or acknowledge a fault.

clue.text: Terrorise drunk? It's just another drunk, probably

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the word reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk menacing people is just another boozer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'drunk' is the anagram signal; the second is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy reveller on a spree is very likely to be a drinker.

clue.text: Girl, quiet rather than loud, dances

indicators.note: rather than says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: Frances is a girl's name
F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A girl who used to be noisy now dances quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to dance or leap about in a lively, showy way.

clue.text: Blade's energy leading to slash

indicators.note: leading to puts the energy letter in front

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
slash is slang for urinating

explanation.surface: A sword's force leads to a cutting stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword, a kind of blade.

clue.text: Exciting interaction with cad? Suggest the opposite

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrilling exchange with a bounder, then a warning to steer clear.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine, to contraindicate a treatment is to show it is inadvisable, pointing the opposite way.

clue.text: Serving area with food receiving a tense reply

indicators.note: receiving means the pair of pieces takes the short letters inside

parts.note: a counter is where food or goods are served
tack is old slang for food, as in hardtack
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A canteen counter, food and a tense moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving area' and 'food' look like the definition's scene; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterattack is an attack made in response, a forceful reply.

clue.text: Chance to run after a fellow-criminal

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the a

parts.note: a bet is a chance or gamble
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A crook's sidekick gets a chance to run off after a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor helps or encourages someone to commit a crime, an accomplice.

clue.text: Pays for checkout item — keeping queue at this?

parts.note: to stand a round is to pay for it
a till is the cash register at a checkout

explanation.surface: At the supermarket, someone pays at the till while the line goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' looks like a containment signal, but belongs to the definition: a queue kept at a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where nothing moves, which is how a stalled queue stays.

clue.text: Make corrupt alteration to clue with speed

indicators.note: alteration to means the letters of the word clue are changed around

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: A setter hastily changes a clue and spoils it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ulcerate is to become sore and festering, hence to corrupt or putrefy.

clue.text: Send tapes with evidence of editing skill

indicators.note: evidence of editing suggests these letters have been cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: Submitting recordings to show off one's editing ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adept means being skilled, so adeptness is skilfulness.

clue.text: Begrudges abandoning new in returns to old position

indicators.note: abandoning means dropping the letter for new

parts.note: to resent something is to begrudge it

explanation.surface: Someone resentful refuses anything new and goes back to the old ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a dial or bone is to put it back where it was.

clue.text: Pest contributing to withdrawal of pest estimates

indicators.note: withdrawal of says the hidden letters are read backwards
contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An insect plays its part in scrapping figures for pest numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly of Africa spreads sleeping sickness, a notorious pest.

clue.text: Man on foot, tinker, bridging river

indicators.note: bridging means the word for tinker spans across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to tamper is to tinker or meddle
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A walker and a travelling tinker cross a bridge over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramper is someone who walks long distances, a hiker.

clue.text: Successful criminal, disposing of drug while getting round rule

indicators.note: getting round means the shortened word wraps around the letter for rule
disposing of means removing the letter for the drug

parts.note: thieving means stealing, criminal
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
R is the abbreviation for rule, as in rex/regina

explanation.surface: A crook does well by ditching the drugs and dodging the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriving business is flourishing, doing well.

clue.text: Meat served up in function held in November?

indicators.note: served up, in a down clue, sends the letters upward so they read backwards
held in puts the function inside the month abbreviation

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A dinner function in November serves game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reads the combined letters NOSINEV from the bottom of the light upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food.

clue.text: Deplorable rejecting Ravel's finale in slow movement — deplorable behaviour

indicators.note: rejecting means the word for deplorable is thrown back, reading in reverse

parts.note: a sad state of affairs is a deplorable one

indicators.note: in puts the composer's last letter inside slowness

parts.note: tardiness is slowness in moving

indicators.note: finale picks the final letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A dismal concert: the Ravel ending dropped from a slow movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slow movement' looks musical, as does 'finale', but means lateness. 'rejecting' reverses SAD to DAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastardly conduct is mean, cowardly wickedness.

clue.text: Clear Spanish hero will ditch Spain, adopting Uruguay initially

indicators.note: adopting means taking the letter in, inside the shortened name
will ditch means the letter for Spain is dropped

parts.note: El Cid is the medieval Spanish hero
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the country

explanation.surface: A Spanish hero quits his homeland for South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid writing is clear and easy to understand.

clue.text: A success supporting second food crop

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, places the later pieces underneath the first

parts.note: a go can mean a success, as in make a go of it

explanation.surface: A successful harvest comes in second.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch taken from palm pith, grown as a food crop.

clue.text: Computer program freezes after opening — cool learning experience

indicators.note: after puts the freezes piece behind the opening piece

parts.note: an app is a computer program
a rent is a tear or opening
ices means freezes
hip means cool or trendy

explanation.surface: Software crashes at launch, a cool lesson in computing.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprenticeship is a period of training under a skilled worker, learning on the job.

clue.text: Couple that'll pick up anything when going North

indicators.note: pick up, in a down clue, lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A pair of scavengers grab anything on a trip north.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT means 'anything' in Yorkshire and northern English speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, two of something.

clue.text: Lady disheartened after writing in suitable terms?

indicators.note: after puts the outer letters behind the writing word

parts.note: corresponding means writing letters to one another

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart of the word, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A woman grows dejected after a letter in suitably formal language.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondingly means in a matching or equivalent way, in terms that suit.
